sentences.transcript: Yellow Clover by Catherine Lee Bates, RadfordLibraVox .org
by Phil Schempf.
Must I, who walk alone, come on at still?
This pup of plants the wise would do away with?
The sunshine slants to play with?
Our wee gold dusty flower, the yellow Clover, which once imparting for a time, that then seemed long, airtime for you was over.
We sealed our own.
Do you remember yet, O soul beyond the stars?
Beyond the utmost dim bars of space?
Dear soul, who found earth sweet?
Remember by love's grace, in dreamy hushes of the heavenly song?
How suddenly we halted in our climb?
Lingering, reluctant.
Up that farthest hill, stooped for the blossoms closest to our feet, and gave them as a token each to each, in lieu of speech, in lieu of words to grievous to be spoken.
Those little gypsy, wondering blossoms, wet with a strange dew of tears.
So it began, this vagabond, unvalued yellow Clover, to be our tenderest language.
All the years it lent a new zest to the summer hours, as each of us went scheming, to surprise the other with our only laureate flowers.
Sonnets and oeds fringing our daily roads.
Can Amorant and Asphodel bring Mary or laughter to your eyes?
Oh, if the blessed, in their serena boats, keep any wistful conscience of earth, not granders, but the childish ways of love, simplicities of mirth.
Must follow them above with touches of vague homesickness, that pass like shadows of swift birds across the grass.

Beneath some foreign arch of sky, how many a time the rover you were I, for life off -sundered look from look, and voice from voice, the transient earth schooling my soul, to brook this distance that no messages may span, would chance upon our wilding by a lonely well, or drowsy watermelon, or swaying to the chime of convent bell, or where the nightingales of old romance with tragic contraltoes failed dim solitudes of infinite desire, and once I joyed to meet our peasant gait about, a trespasser on trim, signorial seat, twinkling a saucy eye as potentates paste by.
Our golden cord, our soft pursuing flame from friendship's altar fire, how proudly we would pluck and tame the dimpling clusters, mutinously gai.

How swiftly they were sent far, far away, on journey's wide, by sea and continent, green miles and blue leagues over, from each of us to each, that our hearts might reach and touch within the yellow clover.
Loves letter to be glad about like sunshine when it came.
My sorrow asks no healing, it is love, let love then make me brave to bear the keen hurts of this careless summer tide.
I, of our own poor flower, changed with our fatal hour, for all its sunshine vanished when you died, only white clover blossoms on your grave.
